Whether an exercise is a main lift decides two things: the workout’s Felt easy / Felt hard prompt (accessories only) and Exercise detail’s graph (est. 1RM for a main lift, weight for an accessory). Progress already shows “the active program’s main lifts”. Claude suggested the program alone decides; owner (2026-11-25): “i feel like this may need to be edited though on an exercise level.” Both options add Lift type to Edit exercise, under Equipment.

The same in both: the app’s segmented control and a line under it; the sheet a little taller. Drawn on Back Squat, a main lift in Pillars. What differs: whether the program has a say.

36aMain lift · Accessory, on the exercise onlyRejected · 36b locked
One answer per exercise, the same in every program. A program’s main lifts are simply the main lifts it contains. Simple, but a program can’t treat Front Squat as a main lift while another treats it as an accessory.
36bFrom program · Main lift · AccessoryLocked · from program
From program by default: the program you are running decides, and the line says what it says (“Pillars has it as a main lift”). Main lift or Accessory overrides it in every program. Programs keep their say; you can still correct one.

Claude’s suggestion: 36b. Programs written with main lifts and their progression work untouched, and the exercise-level edit is there when a program gets it wrong for you. Owner (2026-11-25): “Yeah B.” Locked: 36b. Built into the Exercise Detail Demo.

35Edit exercise · the progression step

The workout’s “Felt easy. Go to 170 lb?” and “Felt hard twice. Drop to 160 lb?” move the weight by the exercise’s own step (locked 2026-11-24; agreed home: Edit exercise; 5 lb by default, as in the current app). Edit exercise has Name, Body part, Equipment and Note today. The step goes under Equipment, with one line saying what it does.

The same in all three: the label “Progression step”, 5 lb picked, the line under it, and the sheet a little taller (still only as tall as its fields). Every exercise has it, since an exercise can be a main lift in one program and an accessory in another; only accessories use it in the workout. A timed exercise shows seconds instead (5 · 10 · 15 sec), and kg users see kg. Drawn on Back Squat, the demo’s exercise. What differs: the control.

35aA capsule that opens a menu, as EquipmentRejected · 35b locked
The same control as Equipment right above it: tap, pick from the menu (2.5, 5, 10, 15, 20 lb). Room for any number of steps, but the value is one tap and a menu away, with the chevron and drop-down.
35bThree segments: 2.5 · 5 · 10 lbLocked · segments
Every choice on screen, one tap to change, the app’s segmented style. Covers microplates (2.5), most barbell and dumbbell work (5) and machine stacks (10); no 15 or 20.
35cA stepper: − 5 lb +Rejected · 35b locked
Any multiple of 2.5 lb. The iOS stepper; flexible, but several taps for a big jump, and the only stepper in the app.

Claude’s suggestion: 35b. Three choices cover almost every exercise, nothing is hidden behind a menu, and it matches the segmented controls already in the app. For a timed exercise, 5 sec by default (the step hold times already move in). Owner (2026-11-25): “yeah i think B too.” Locked: 35b. Built into the Exercise Detail Demo. The timed default is still open.

34Exercise detail · the accessory graph, live: reps or RPE

After turn 33 (owner): leaning B, but there needs to be a focus on the graph: press and drag to select a data point, and the shaded block / program too. Probably needs averages on longer time periods. Reps as the bars might be better than RPE; see both.

Both are live: drag the graph and switch ranges. Up to 30 sessions in range, one bar per session (Program, 6M). Past that, one bar per month showing that month's average (1Y, All), and the readout gives the month: sessions, average reps, average RPE. The weight line is never averaged. Blocks become programs past 10 blocks, as on a main lift. No snapping or haptic: there are no PR dots to snap to. The 30-session cut-off is Claude's placeholder.

23Resources · adding a link, and rows without a thumbnail

After turn 22 (owner): leaning to the rows card (22a). The app might ship with some links, but assume blank. What does Add link look like, what happens when you press it? Can we get thumbnails for each (YouTube probably; Instagram, TikTok?), and what does the row look like when we can't?

Static mocks. Thumbnails would come from iOS's own link-preview fetch (what Messages uses), which reads the title and image the page itself publishes; no per-site API. YouTube reliably has both; Instagram and TikTok often give a title but not always an image, hence states 3 and 4.

20Sessions · 19a decluttered, and what a tap opens

After turn 19 (owner): 19a definitely looks better, the best so far, though a little messy and cluttered. What happens when you tap a row? Claude proposed: it opens that session's Session detail (the same screen as from History and Calendar), scrolled to this exercise with a brief highlight. Owner: see it, with a less cluttered 19a, before moving on.

Both phones are the Back Squat Sessions page. Tap any row: Session detail slides in (a stand-in for the system push), already scrolled past the top card to Back Squat, which shows a thin accent outline that fades out over about two seconds; back returns to the list where you were. The squat card uses that row's real sets; the rest of the session is the Session Detail Demo's layout with placeholder exercises. Beside each phone, the same rows in the Exercise detail card, main lift and accessory.

How it's calculated
Est. 1RM
The most you could lift once, estimated from each working set's weight and reps. Warm-ups don't count.
Now
The average of your 3 best sessions in the range, so one great or bad day can't move it alone.
Change
Your 3 best in this range against your 3 best before it. On Program: against the same point in your last block of the same type.
Line
Each session, smoothed over 3 sessions so deloads and off days don't look like drops. Under 8 sessions, every session is shown as it is.
Best so far
Your highest est. 1RM to date. It steps up at every PR (the green dots). Dashed when this range has no PR.
Your real lifts
What you actually did at 1, 3, 5, 8, 12 and 15 reps is in Rep records below.
